environmentalPersistence: Moderate — atmospheric half-life ~2 days via OH radical; moderate soil persistence

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Moderate — slightly less toxic than benzene; similar mechanism via aromatic metabolites
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Moderate — margin necrosis similar to benzene but slightly less severe
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Older leaves show chlorosis first; uniform effects at high dose

physiologyEffects.membranePermeability: Increased — lipophilic aromatic ring disrupts bilayer

visualSimulation.damagePattern: Marginal necrosis with chlorotic background — very similar to benzene
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Moderate orange — MDA and cresol metabolite signature

synergies.synergyNote: BTEX mixture (benzene + toluene + ethylbenzene + xylene) is a classic indoor/industrial pollutant combo — synergistic GSH depletion and membrane disruption

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Paint, nail polish remover, gasoline, adhesives, industrial solvents — extremely common indoor and outdoor pollutant
educationalContext.humanToxicity: High — neurotoxin at high concentrations; reproductive toxin; suspected carcinogen
educationalContext.climateLink: Major component of urban smog precursor emissions
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Both — major indoor source from paints and adhesives; outdoor from traffic
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: In nail polish, paint, and markers — products students use regularly. The neurotoxicity angle is immediately impactful.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Indoor air quality, occupational health, urban air pollution
